steps: The Wish of a Single Grain
Upon the throne, you make a wish beyond imagination. The companions' souls struggle to break free, and Noya calls out her own name. The chance to settle things with Coppelius has finally arrived...
A-Are you okay? Um... Do you remember us?
Yo... Yonon... Wait, Yonon!? And everyone else too...! Why are you here? Is everyone okay!?
Ahaha... I don't think we're "okay" the way you want, 18. Oh, sorry. You go by "Alina" now, right?
Anyway, um... It's not like we can really see you, Alina... We can't hear you clearly either.
Hmm... How should I put this? We're just ... here, fighting a different opponent every day…
You've received a name. Have you been happy?
... I'm sorry. Please don't call me by that name. "Alina" isn't a name I ever wanted.
And… Getting a name doesn't really change anything. Whether it's "Alina" or "18," they're all just what others decide to call me on their own.
In that sense... Maybe the days since I left Emor have been no different from fighting in a new arena every day.
But enough about that...==W== There's something I need to apologize to you...==W== I was the one managed to get out of the arena, and yet...==W== When I went back to bring you out... It was too late…
Heh... Honestly, 18. What's with that gloom? It's not like you.
You know, we were actually watching when you put up those gravestones for us.
So, 18, thank you for remembering us, and for always keeping us with you.
Also, because you carved it on the gravestone, the name "Yonon" started to feel like a real name to me now.
Oh, and... Though you said it makes no difference whether you're "No. 18" or "Alina"...
A real name lies in the heart of the person who calls you by it. It's all that matters, isn't it?
Yeah. Because when you were carving "Yonon" into that gravestone, what you felt must be so complicated, yet so sincere... And that's exactly why it made me so happy…
To us, that felt far more precious than getting recognized by the Priests or the Archons.
So... You don't need to apologize to us, 18, nor do you need to worry about bringing us back. What you should wish for is—
Whether you are the God of Grace,==W== the Monolith itself,==W== or something else entirely... It doesn't matter.
I hereby wish that from this day forth—
All intelligent beings shall be born free, and equal.
What I should wish for is…
Hey, 18, did you know?! They say if you go into that tower and make a wish, then any wish will come true!
"Please don't let me be born a slave ever again in my next life..." Do you think a wish like that would work?
No use thinking about it. It's only for Senators, Priests, and Saintesses. Gladiators have no place there.
I know, I know. A little wishful thinking doesn't hurt. If we ever survive this, maybe one of us would get lucky someday?
And if one of us does make it into the tower... They could wish on our behalf! "Please don't let any of us be born a slave in our next lives"!
—Yes, I know. About that, you don't need to worry.
Our wish ... will definitely come true.
Heh, sounds like you've found some good friends, huh?
Well, if that's settled for the wish... What should we call you then, if not "18" or "Alina"?
"Noya"... That's what I'd like you to call me.
Someday, I want to be like ==SEX3== friend, to become someone remarkable, so I borrowed the name. Heh... In the end, it still isn't a name that belongs to me...

==Off== Yes. It's a name you chose yourself.
So "Noya" is the name you wanted. A name that's yours alone! You don't have to hold back for anyone! After all, there's only one you in this whole world!
Come on, Noya, be proud! You gave yourself that name because you want to become a better self. That makes it the best name ever, right?
Once, we were as small and insignificant as the grains of sand in the arena.
Each grain was so fragile it could vanish in an instant...
But even they're tiny, when they come together...
They can build a towering wall and defeat even the strongest enemy!
18... Noya, you've proved it to us again and again!
All right, you two, draw your swords once more. This is our very last battle in the arena, and we're going to win!
Yeah. Being looked down on all this time is infuriating. Let's show him we're not just his pet dogs.
I'm sick and tired of being a slave! No one's gonna order me around ever again!
W-Wait. What... What are you going to do?
If you defy Coppelius, his magic will consume you!
Yeah. And that's exactly why. We never did get our freedom, but... At least at the very end, we wanted to choose for ourselves.
Hey, 18. Even after you were left all alone, you never stopped, and you carried us so very far.
But this isn't the end of the journey. I know you're going to keep trekking, even further from here.
Don't worry, Noya. As long as you don't forget us... We'll never, ever disappear! Come on, everyone, let's go!!
Phew... That should do for first aid.
You three, go fetch some lumber and assemble a slave's crucifix right here. Before I skin her alive, she will pay the price she deserves.
… Hm? Why aren't you moving? Fetch the wood and build the crucifix.
In the Monoliths, may everyone pursue the future they envision!
In the Monoliths, may no one be forced to make a wish against their will!
From the past to the present, any wish born of deception, persecution, or any other inequality shall be decided anew by the one who made it.
(There should be no flaws in the puppets I made with the tower's power. And yet, why on earth are they disobeying my orders? Could it be...)
(The tower's light is ... flickering? Is someone making a wish inside...?)
(That voice... The Fallen Saintess...!? How did she break free of my magic...? No, more importantly, this incantation. Oh, no! She's seizing control of the magic circle!)
(Ngh... It seems I underestimated them. Alina's assassination attempt was merely a stall for time. Their true target was the tower and the magic circle all along...)
To think that I would be toyed with by useless wretches who can't even use magic properly... How humiliating!
My plans have gone awry, but... I'll crucify every last one of you. First the Saintess, then on to the tower—
I won't let you have your way!!
... And as for those three, they won't obey you anymore. They've all ... determined their own fate!
Coppelius, you're going to pay for this...==W== And the price will be enormous.
I-Impossible...! There's no way you could take my blow head-on and come out unscathed! But why!? How are you still standing!?
You're right. Every bone in my body might already be broken.
But... I'll get back up as many times as it takes. Heh, you want to know why?
In the duel against the puppets,==W== my friends joined hands to protect me==W== and gave me the chance to fight to the very end.
But... Even after the duel was over, I always wondered. Was my life really worth their sacrifice...
It's pathetic, but... It's only now that I finally understand. The reason I survived, and the meaning of this life. And that is—
No matter how many times I'm knocked down, I'll rise every time... To protect the ones who fight alongside me, and fulfill the dearest wish of the perished!
Laughable! Your insignificant lives and meaningless ideals are nothing but dust before Archon Olympia and me.
Did you think that cutting off the tower's magic would let you defeat me? How unfortunate. There isn't a chance in a million that you could ever defeat us.
It's true that to you, our lives may be nothing more than worthless grains of sand.
But...==W== Crush them tens of thousands, even hundreds of thousands of times, all that remains is still grain.
Listen well, Coppelius, and remember this!
My name is Noya! Born of the arena—
And I'm the grain of sand that will bury you right here!
